questions.q:
A design team is about to start developing a new range of products. Part of this process is the implementation of management plans.

These plans ensure that the products
options: meet the intended purpose.
address all legal requirements.
are developed on time and on budget.
meet the needs of the target market.
questions.explanation: The three management plans are action, time and finance — ATF. They sequence work on a Gantt chart and track the budget so the project is delivered on time and on budget. Meeting the purpose, legal needs and the target market are achieved through other parts of the design process.

questions.q: Why do designers establish and review 'criteria to evaluate success' when designing?
options: To increase the number of sales of a product
To ensure environmental factors are considered
To ensure the final design meets the specified needs
To maintain product awareness for further refinement of innovative products
questions.explanation: Criteria to evaluate success are the measurable benchmarks set in the proposal (NICe) and judged against at the end — the great bookend of the MDP. They exist to confirm the final design meets the specified need. The other options are narrower commercial or environmental concerns.

questions.q: Distinguish between the factors affecting design and the factors affecting the success of an innovation.
options: They are the same set of factors, simply renamed for the innovation case study

The factors affecting design are the eleven considerations weighed in any project (FFA EQ NEW LOAd, H1.1), while the factors affecting innovation success are a separate set of six (TEMPLE, H3.1) concerning market success
The factors affecting design number six and concern market success; the innovation factors number eleven and concern the design itself
The design factors apply only to the folio, while the innovation factors apply only to the prototype
questions.explanation: This is the headline trap-buster: the eleven factors affecting design (FFA EQ NEW LOAd, H1.1) concern the design itself, whereas the six factors affecting an innovation's success (TEMPLE, H3.1, met in module H2) concern the conditions for market success. Keep the two sets separate.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a work health and safety (WHS) risk assessment?
options: To identify dangerous equipment
To evaluate workshop organisation and practices
To access the impact of materials on the environment
To identify and assess potential injury or illness in the workplace
questions.explanation: A risk assessment systematically identifies hazards and assesses the potential for injury or illness so they can be controlled through the hierarchy of control. It is the first step in managing safety — identifying dangerous equipment is only one part of that broader process.

questions.q: In the hierarchy of control, where does personal protective equipment (PPE) sit, and why?
options: First, because PPE is the quickest way to remove a hazard for everyone
Last resort, because PPE only protects the wearer whereas elimination removes the hazard for everyone
It is not part of the hierarchy of control at all
Equal first with elimination, since both fully remove the risk
questions.explanation: The hierarchy runs eliminate, substitute, engineering controls, administrative controls, and finally PPE. PPE is the last resort because it protects only the wearer, while eliminating a hazard removes it for everyone. Answering a safety question with PPE first is a classic exam trap.

questions.q: Why does a designer need to consider the industrial and commercial practices that will be used during manufacturing?
options: To ensure the product will sell
To gain access to cheaper resources
To increase the product's rate of production
To produce products that meet market needs
questions.explanation: Relating industrial and commercial practice (SPPC — safe work, production techniques, process selection, collaborative teams) lets a designer plan for efficient mass production and a higher rate of production. The other options are commercial outcomes that depend on, but are not the direct reason for, considering these practices.

questions.q: From memory: what does the project proposal contain, what are the three management plans, and what is the justify-not-narrate pattern?
keyPoints: The proposal contains NICe — the Need (identified and analysed), the areas of Investigation to research, and the measurable Criteria for success (functional and aesthetic).
The three management plans are Action, Time (a Gantt chart) and Finance — ATF.
The justify pattern is decision, reason, factor, evidence: state the decision, give the reason, name the factor (from FFA EQ NEW LOAd), cite the evidence. Justify, don't narrate.
questions.explanation: These three — the proposal, the management plans and the justify pattern — are the spine of the module. If you recalled all three, grade yourself Good or Easy.

questions.q: From memory: across what three levels is the impact of a major design project assessed, and what must a strong impact answer do?
keyPoints: Impact is assessed across three levels — Individual, Society and Environment (ISE).

At each level, weigh both costs and benefits (e.g. a useful product for the individual at its purchase price; a community benefit for society against resource use; an environmental footprint reducible by renewable, recyclable materials).
Conclude with an overall, balanced judgement of the net impact — a one-sided or single-level answer caps low.
questions.explanation: ISE is the evaluation-of-impact hook (H4.3), and the same skill scales up to H2.2 for innovations. If you named all three levels and remembered to balance costs against benefits with a final judgement, grade yourself Good or Easy.

questions.q:
A designer has been asked to produce a working prototype of a desk lamp that uses a variety of materials.

Outline safe work practices that should be implemented by the designer during the development of the prototype.
questions.modelAnswer: A risk assessment should be conducted before constructing the prototype, and personal protective equipment (PPE) used to minimise injury — for example a face mask and eye protection (goggles, safety glasses) to guard against dust and flying particles when cutting wood for the lamp stand, and hearing protection when sawing. Electrical work on the lamp should be carried out and tagged by a licensed technician, and materials should be tested to ensure no toxic fumes are emitted. Tools and machinery should be regularly maintained and inspected, and suitable training (SOP/SLMS and MSDS sheets) undertaken before use.

criteria.descriptor: Outlines safe work practices that should be implemented by the designer with a direct link to the desk lamp
Identifies safe work practices that should be implemented by the designer and outlines at least one of them
Identifies safe work practices OR outlines one safe work practice

questions.explanation: Anchor the answer in the hierarchy of control — eliminate and engineer out hazards before relying on PPE — and tie each practice directly to the desk lamp (cutting, sawing, electrical work) to reach full marks. This same answer scores in H4.2 and H6.1.

questions.q: Describe how action plans and ongoing evaluation processes work together to contribute to the development of a successful design.
questions.modelAnswer: As part of the design process the designer develops an action plan to organise an appropriate and efficient operation, sequencing tasks correctly so the project runs efficiently. Combined with an ongoing evaluation structure, this helps ensure a successful design: if ongoing evaluation is not carried out, development may fail to address concerns about important design factors such as function, cost or safety. Together, action plans and ongoing evaluation ensure the end product best meets the needs of the client and the consumer.

criteria.descriptor: Provides characteristics and features of how action plans AND ongoing evaluation processes work together to contribute to a successful design
Provides characteristics and features of how action plans AND/OR evaluation processes contribute to a successful design
Sketches in general terms how action plans AND/OR evaluation processes contribute to a successful design, OR identifies a feature of action plans AND a feature of evaluation processes
Identifies a feature of action plans OR evaluation processes

questions.explanation: Show the link both ways: the action plan (the A in ATF) sequences and times the work, while continual evaluation — before, mid and after (BMA) — checks progress against the criteria and drives refinement. Describing one in isolation caps in the middle.
